learn.term.broker.name: Broker
learn.term.broker.def: The window that charts one ticker and places orders. You can open up to four, one per ticker.
learn.term.ticket.name: Ticket
learn.term.ticket.def: The order form inside a Broker: side, order type, quantity and price. Only Enter in the Broker sends an order.
learn.term.ticker.name: Ticker
learn.term.ticker.def: The short code for a tradable asset, such as HLCN. Each ticker has its own chart, news and price.
learn.term.market_order.name: Market order
learn.term.market_order.def: Buys or sells now, at the best price available.
learn.term.limit_order.name: Limit order
learn.term.limit_order.def: Buys or sells only at your price or better. It waits until the market gets there.
learn.term.stop_order.name: Stop order
learn.term.stop_order.def: Waits until the price reaches your stop price, then sells or buys at market. Often used to cap a loss.
learn.term.stop_limit.name: Stop-limit order
learn.term.stop_limit.def: A stop order that then places a limit order at your limit price, so it fills at that price or better, or not at all.
learn.term.trailing_stop.name: Trailing stop
learn.term.trailing_stop.def: A stop that follows the price by a set percentage. It sells if the price falls that far from its best level since you placed it.
learn.term.position.name: Position
learn.term.position.def: The shares you hold in one asset, with your average cost.
learn.term.cash.name: Cash
learn.term.cash.def: Money you can spend now. Buying takes cash, and selling adds it back.
learn.term.net_worth.name: Net worth
learn.term.net_worth.def: Cash plus everything you hold, at today’s prices. It is the figure in the status strip.
learn.term.unrealized_gain.name: Unrealized gain
learn.term.unrealized_gain.def: Profit or loss on shares you still hold. It moves with the price until you sell.
learn.term.fee.name: Fee
learn.term.fee.def: A charge taken from cash on each trade. Fees differ by asset class.
learn.term.slippage.name: Slippage
learn.term.slippage.def: The gap between the price you expected and the price you got. Large orders in thin markets move the price against you.
learn.term.margin.name: Margin
learn.term.margin.def: Borrowed money that lets you buy more than your cash covers. You pay interest. A margin call comes below 30% equity, and the broker sells for you below 20%.
learn.term.short.name: Short
learn.term.short.def: Selling shares you do not own, by borrowing them, so you profit if the price falls. You buy them back later.
learn.term.option.name: Option
learn.term.option.def: A contract to buy (a call) or sell (a put) an asset at a fixed strike before expiry. The most you can lose is the premium you paid.
learn.term.strike.name: Strike
learn.term.strike.def: The fixed price in an option. A call pays when the price ends above it; a put pays when it ends below.
learn.term.expiry.name: Expiry
learn.term.expiry.def: The day an option ends. It settles in cash at that day’s close.
learn.term.wire.name: Wire
learn.term.wire.def: The news feed: headlines, world events, milestones and rival moves, newest first.
learn.term.rumor.name: Rumor
learn.term.rumor.def: An unconfirmed story. Rumors are right most of the time, but not always.
learn.term.priced_in.name: Priced in
learn.term.priced_in.def: How much of a news move has already happened. Early means most of it is still to come; Priced in means it is done.
learn.term.earnings.name: Earnings
learn.term.earnings.def: A company’s quarterly report of profit and sales. How it beats or misses expectations moves the price.
learn.term.analyst.name: Analyst
learn.term.analyst.def: A paid helper that explains your closed trades: the market, the sector, the news and the fees.
learn.term.world_event.name: World event
learn.term.world_event.def: A market-wide event, such as a storm or a major shock. The biggest ones take over the screen for a moment.
learn.term.sector.name: Sector
learn.term.sector.def: A group of companies in the same business, such as tech or energy. Sectors often move together.
learn.term.volatility.name: Volatility
learn.term.volatility.def: How far prices swing, up and down. High volatility means bigger moves in both directions.
learn.term.day.name: Game day
learn.term.day.def: One day in the game. A day order expires at the end of that day, and the status strip shows the day and the time.
learn.term.rank.name: Rank
learn.term.rank.def: Your standing in the game, from Broke up to Dynasty. Each rank unlocks apps and workspaces.
learn.term.prestige.name: Prestige
learn.term.prestige.def: Status points from lifestyle purchases and homes. You see them in Boutique.
learn.term.business.name: Business
learn.term.business.def: Something you own that earns income every game day. Away for more than 12 hours, it slows down unless you automate it.
learn.term.contract.name: Contract
learn.term.contract.def: A goal with a reward. You get three each game day; claim the reward once it is done.
learn.term.license.name: License
learn.term.license.def: A permission that unlocks a kind of trade, such as options with the Derivatives license. Settings shows your licenses.
learn.term.company.name: Company

learn.lesson.setup: This lesson starts you with one unit of {asset}, bought and filled.
learn.lesson.hint.market-fill: Place a market order for one unit, then advance one game day so it fills.
learn.lesson.hint.limit-wait: Place a limit order with a price below the current price. It stays open.
learn.lesson.hint.stop-below: Place a stop order below the current price for the unit you hold.
learn.lesson.hint.held-day: Keep the unit you hold and advance one more game day.
learn.lesson.hint.fee-seen: Place a market order for one unit, then advance one game day. The fees appear in the figures above.
learn.lesson.hint.over-cash: Enter a quantity your cash cannot cover, then place the order.
learn.lesson.hint.short-refused: Try an order for a unit you do not hold, then place it.
learn.lesson.hint.held-days: Keep the unit for five game days, advancing the market each time.
learn.lesson.hint.round-trip: Add one unit twice, advance a day, then close the whole position with one order.
learn.lesson.1.read: A market order fills at the market price on the following tick. It does not wait for a price you set.
learn.lesson.1.task: Place a market order for one unit, then advance one game day.
learn.lesson.1.done: It filled at the market price, and the position now shows in the figures above.
learn.lesson.2.read: A limit order sets the price you accept. If the market has not reached it, the order waits in the open orders list.
learn.lesson.2.task: Place a limit order with a price below the current price, and leave it open.
learn.lesson.2.done: It waits until the market reaches your price. Until then it holds no shares.
learn.lesson.3.read: A stop order waits until the price reaches your stop price, then turns into a market order. Traders often use one to cap a loss on a position they hold.
learn.lesson.3.task: You hold one unit. Place a stop order below the current price for that unit.
learn.lesson.3.done: The stop triggers only when the price reaches its level.
learn.lesson.4.read: A position’s value follows its price. The price moves with the whole market, its sector, the news and the company’s own results. Its gain or loss stays unrealized until you close the position.
learn.lesson.4.task: You hold one unit. Advance one game day and watch the position’s figures.
learn.lesson.4.done: The change came from the price. The result becomes realized only when you close the position.
learn.lesson.5.read: Every fill pays a fee taken from cash. The gap between the bid and ask prices is a cost too. Both count against your result from the first trade.
learn.lesson.5.task: Place a market order for one unit, then advance one game day. Look at the fees paid.
learn.lesson.5.done: Fees are part of your result from the first trade.
learn.lesson.6.read: Margin is borrowed money. A plain account can spend only its cash, so an order larger than its cash is refused. With margin, a position that falls too far can be closed for you.
learn.lesson.6.task: Place the market order with the large quantity shown. The sandbox refuses it: your cash cannot cover it.
learn.lesson.6.done: A plain account can only spend the cash it has.
learn.lesson.7.read: A short sale borrows shares and sells them now, so you gain if the price falls. The shares must be returned later. This practice account cannot short. In the game, a short is secured by your own cash from the start.
learn.lesson.7.task: Place a sell order for one unit you do not hold. The sandbox refuses it.
learn.lesson.7.done: This practice account holds only cash. In the game, a short is secured by your own cash from the start.
learn.lesson.8.read: Some companies pay a dividend: a share of profit paid in cash to holders. A DRIP, set per position in the Broker, uses each dividend to buy more of the same stock.
learn.lesson.8.task: You hold one unit. Advance five game days.
learn.lesson.8.done: Dividends arrive as cash. A DRIP reinvests them when you turn it on for a position.
learn.lesson.9.read: A round trip opens with your first fill and closes when the position returns to zero. While you hold, your average cost is the average of your fills, with fees included.
learn.lesson.9.task: Add one unit twice, advance a day, then close the whole position with one order.
learn.lesson.9.done: The round trip is closed, and its result is realized.
learn.lesson.10.read: Each game day ends with a close. Prices settle, net worth is marked at the close, and your daily close card sums up the day.
learn.lesson.10.done: The close marks your net worth for the day.

luck.explain.1: Luck and skill look alike over a few weeks. The ghosts show what three simple rules would have done with the same starting cash.
luck.explain.2: Index basket: the market index, weighted by company size, bought once and held. Random picks: {picks} stocks drawn at random, redrawn every {days} game days. Momentum: the {picks} stocks that rose most over the last {momentum} game days, redrawn the same way.
luck.explain.3: Ghosts pay no fees or spread and trade at closing prices. Your number already includes what your trading cost, so the gap is a fair test of your choices. A few weeks can still come down to chance, so one result proves little.

company.refusal.notRank.what: Founding a company needs the Owner rank.
company.refusal.notRank.do: Keep growing your net worth until you reach Owner.
company.refusal.capitalTooLow.what: That capital is too small to found a company.
company.refusal.capitalTooLow.why: The founder equity must reach the minimum.
company.refusal.capitalTooLow.do: Put in more capital and try again.
company.refusal.alreadyFounded.why: Each player has one company in this version.
company.refusal.insufficientFunds.what: You do not have enough cash.
company.refusal.insufficientFunds.why: The cash you have is short by {shortfall}.
company.refusal.insufficientFunds.do: Sell something, or wait for your cash to build up.
company.refusal.unknownCompany.why: It may never have been founded.
company.refusal.unknownCompany.do: Open your company list and pick one you run.
company.refusal.notFounder.what: Only the founder can run this company.
company.refusal.notFounder.why: This company belongs to another player.
company.refusal.headcountCap.what: The company is at its headcount cap.
company.refusal.headcountCap.why: At this tier the cap is {cap} heads, counting people still joining.
company.refusal.headcountCap.do: Hire fewer people, or wait for the company to reach the next tier.
company.refusal.notEnoughStaff.what: There are not that many people to let go in this role.
company.refusal.notEnoughStaff.why: Only seated staff can be let go.
company.refusal.noRdStaff.what: No R&D staff are ready to work.
company.refusal.noRdStaff.why: A project needs productive R&D heads, and new hires take 21 game days to ramp.
company.refusal.noRdStaff.do: Hire R&D staff and wait for them to ramp.
company.refusal.projectBusy.why: The company runs one R&D project at a time.
company.refusal.projectBusy.do: Wait for it to finish, then start the next.
company.refusal.productCap.do: Grow to the next tier before you launch more.
company.refusal.unknownProduct.why: It may belong to another company.
company.refusal.unknownProduct.do: Pick a product from your own line.
company.refusal.priceOutOfBand.what: That price is outside the allowed band.
company.refusal.priceOutOfBand.do: Choose a price inside the band.
company.refusal.moneyTooLarge.what: That amount is above the most the company books can hold.
company.refusal.moneyTooLarge.why: Money is kept to the cent, and above {max} the cents can no longer be counted exactly.
company.refusal.negativeAmount.why: Amounts must be positive whole numbers.
company.refusal.roundDilutionCap.what: That round would dilute the founder too far.
company.refusal.roundDilutionCap.why: A private round can sell at most a quarter of the company after the round.
company.refusal.roundAfterListing.what: The company is already listed, so it cannot take a private round.
company.refusal.roundAfterListing.why: Private rounds are for companies before their listing. A listed company's shares trade on the exchange.
company.refusal.roundAfterListing.do: Raise capital from the market instead, through a buyback, a dividend or a new filing.
company.refusal.roundDuringIpo.what: The IPO book is open, so no private round can be raised now.
company.refusal.roundDuringIpo.why: The share count is fixed while the book is open, and the new shares would not match the book.
company.refusal.roundDuringIpo.do: Wait until the company lists, then try again if you still need a round.
company.refusal.investorCash.what: The investors do not have that much cash left.
company.refusal.investorCash.do: Raise a smaller amount, or wait for the next round.
company.refusal.plantBuilding.what: A plant is already being built.
company.refusal.plantBuilding.why: Only one plant can be under construction at a time.
company.refusal.unknownAction.why: The company does not know this action.
company.refusal.unknownAction.do: Refresh the screen and try again.
company.refusal.noValuation.what: The company has no value yet.
company.refusal.noValuation.why: A private round needs a valuation, and the company has no sales yet.
company.refusal.noValuation.do: Make a first sale, then try again.
company.refusal.marketingCap.what: That marketing budget is above the cap.
company.refusal.marketingCap.why: Marketing is capped per product per game day so that no company can buy its share.
company.refusal.marketingCap.do: Set a budget of {cap} or less.
company.refusal.noLaunchCredit.what: No new product is ready to launch.
company.refusal.noLaunchCredit.why: A new product needs a next-gen project that has succeeded and has not been launched yet.
company.refusal.noLaunchCredit.do: Start a next-gen project and wait for it to succeed.
company.refusal.notController.what: Only the controlling owner can do that.
company.refusal.notController.why: Control needs more than half of the votes, and the founder holds them.
company.refusal.notController.do: Act on a company you control.
company.refusal.companyBankrupt.why: Its debts were settled from its own assets, and its stock was delisted.
company.refusal.companyBankrupt.do: Read the bankruptcy notice in your inbox.
company.refusal.ceoChangePending.what: A CEO change is already announced.
company.refusal.ceoChangePending.why: Only one change can be pending, and it cannot be withdrawn once filed.
company.refusal.ceoChangePending.do: Wait until day {untilDay}, when the change takes effect.
company.refusal.exCeoCooling.what: That person cannot take the CEO role yet.
company.refusal.exCeoCooling.why: A former CEO must wait 252 game days before returning to the role.
company.refusal.exCeoCooling.do: Wait until day {untilDay}, when the cooling ends.
company.refusal.ceoExitFreeze.what: Trading is frozen while the CEO change is settled.
company.refusal.ceoExitFreeze.why: The departing CEO cannot trade the stock until the freeze ends, so the change cannot move the price.
company.refusal.ceoExitFreeze.do: Wait until day {untilDay}. Plans set up earlier keep running.
company.refusal.execFilled.what: That seat already has an executive.
company.refusal.execFilled.why: Each seat holds one executive at a time: CEO, CFO, COO or CTO.
company.refusal.execFilled.do: Let the current executive go after the minimum term, or pick another seat.
company.refusal.execNotFound.what: No executive sits in that seat.
company.refusal.execNotFound.why: The seat is empty, so there is no one to let go.
company.refusal.execNotFound.do: Pick a seat that has an executive.
company.refusal.execTerm.what: That executive is still within the minimum term.
company.refusal.execTerm.why: A new executive has a minimum term, and severance is owed if they leave early.
company.refusal.execSalaryCap.what: That salary is above the cap for a player.
company.refusal.execSalaryCap.why: A salary paid to a player is capped at the larger of $50 a game day and 1% of the company's revenue per day.
company.refusal.execSalaryCap.do: Choose a salary within the cap of {cap} a game day.
company.refusal.guaranteeTooHigh.what: That guarantee is larger than you can back.
company.refusal.guaranteeTooHigh.why: A personal guarantee is capped at half of your cash on hand.
company.refusal.boardRejected.what: The board did not approve it.
company.refusal.boardRejected.why: The vote was {yes} for and {no} against, counted by shares. New investors vote no when the price is below fair value.
company.refusal.boardRejected.do: Change the terms and try again.
company.refusal.franchiseRate.what: That royalty rate is outside the allowed range.
company.refusal.franchiseRate.why: An operator pays between {min}% and {max}% of its revenue as royalty.
company.refusal.franchiseRate.do: Choose a rate within the range.
company.refusal.franchiseCap.what: The sector already has as many franchises as it can take.
company.refusal.franchiseCap.why: At most {cap} licences run in one sector, across all companies.
company.refusal.franchiseCap.do: License another sector, or wait for a licence to end.
company.refusal.franchiseNoProduct.what: The brand has no product to license.
company.refusal.franchiseNoProduct.why: An operator licenses a product line, and this company has none.
company.refusal.supplyPriceOutOfBand.wha: That supply price is outside the allowed band.
company.refusal.supplyPriceOutOfBand.why: Supply is priced within 10% of the market reference, between {min} and {max} per unit. A related deal outside the band is also flagged to surveillance.
company.refusal.supplySelf.why: A supply deal needs a buyer and a different seller.
company.refusal.supplySelf.do: Pick another company as the seller.
company.refusal.takeoverNotListed.why: A takeover tender pays every holder of a listed company's stock.
company.refusal.takeoverNoBidder.what: There is no account to pay for the bid.
company.refusal.takeoverNoBidder.why: A tender is paid from the bidder's account, and the holders cannot be paid without one.
company.refusal.takeoverNoBidder.do: Open a trading account, then bid.
company.refusal.takeoverBelowFloor.what: The bid is below the floor.
company.refusal.takeoverBelowFloor.why: A tender must pay at least 1.2 times the company's 30-day average price, measured before the bidder began building its stake.
company.refusal.takeoverUnfunded.what: You cannot pay for the whole tender.
company.refusal.takeoverUnfunded.why: The bid pays every holder at one price, and you are short by {shortfall}.
company.refusal.takeoverUnfunded.do: Add cash to your account, then bid again.
company.refusal.takeoverSelfDeal.what: You cannot bid for a company that shares an owner with you.
company.refusal.takeoverSelfDeal.why: A takeover by your own accounts would be self-dealing.
company.refusal.takeoverSelfDeal.do: Bid as an unrelated account, or bid for another company.
company.refusal.contractPriceOutOfBand.w: That contract's day rate is outside the allowed band.
A contractor is paid within 10% of the market day rate, between {min} and {max} per day. A contract with a player in your owner set that is outside the band is also flagged to surveillance.
company.refusal.contractPriceOutOfBand.d: Set a day rate between {min} and {max}.
company.refusal.contractNotFound.what: That contract does not exist or has ended.
company.refusal.contractNotFound.why: A contract ends at its term, or when a loan is fully repaid.
company.refusal.contractNotFound.do: Pick an open contract from the company's list.
company.refusal.notParty.what: Only the other party to this contract can do that.
company.refusal.notParty.why: A loan from the company is repaid by the player who borrowed it.
company.refusal.notParty.do: Ask the borrower to make the repayment.
company.refusal.loanBalance.what: That amount is more than the loan still owes.
company.refusal.loanBalance.why: A loan can be repaid or prepaid only up to its balance, which is {balance} now.
company.refusal.loanTooSmall.why: A loan to a company is at least {min}, so that its repayment schedule is worth tracking.
company.refusal.guaranteeLocked.what: The guarantee cannot be cut right now.
company.refusal.guaranteeLocked.why: The company is short of the sum the guarantee covers, or in distress, and its creditors rely on the guarantee.
company.refusal.guaranteeLocked.do: Keep the guarantee until the company's cash covers it again.
company.refusal.takeoverNoFloor.what: There is no pre-attack price to set a floor from.
company.refusal.takeoverNoFloor.why: The floor is 1.2 times the company's average price over the 30 game days before the pre-attack start, and it did not trade in that window.
company.refusal.takeoverNoFloor.do: Wait until the company has traded for a month, then bid.
company.refusal.antitrustBlock.what: The combined market share would be too large.
company.refusal.antitrustBlock.why: Together the two companies would hold {share}% of their sector, above the 60% limit.
company.refusal.antitrustBlock.do: Pick a target in another sector, or a smaller company.

funds.mandate.notice: {fund} changes its mandate in {hours} real hours. Redemptions are open without the gate until then.
funds.frozen: {fund} is frozen: its manager has been away for {hours} real hours. Trading is off and redemptions are open without the gate. It winds down in {days} game days unless the manager returns.
funds.thawed: {fund} is open again: its manager is back.
funds.windDown: {fund} is winding down. Its positions go to market and every holder is redeemed at NAV.
funds.closed: {fund} has closed. Every payout is made.
funds.breaker: {fund}'s NAV fell {pct}% from its high in a week. New trades are off for a game day; redemptions are open without the gate.
funds.case.opened: A court case over front-running is open against {fund}'s manager. The evidence so far shows {harm} of harm to the fund.
funds.case.opened.holder: A court case over front-running is open for {fund}'s holders.
funds.court.opened: A fund-abuse case is open against you. The hearing is in {days} game days.
funds.verdict.won: You won against {player}. {restored} goes back into the fund, and the fine is {fine}.
funds.vcf.paid: The Victim Compensation Fund advances you {amount} on your share of the award against {fund}, while the rest is pursued.
funds.verdict.lost: The verdict is against you. {restored} goes back into the fund, the stake first, and the fine is {fine}. You are banned from fund management for 8 real weeks.
funds.refusal.fundNoFund.what: There is no fund by that name.
funds.refusal.fundNoFund.why: It may have closed, or the link is old.
funds.refusal.fundNoFund.do: Pick a fund from the list on the Exchange.
funds.refusal.fundNotManager.what: Only the fund's manager can do that.
funds.refusal.fundNotManager.why: Investors can put money into a fund and redeem their own units.
funds.refusal.fundNotManager.do: Invest or redeem from the fund's page instead.
funds.refusal.fundTerms.what: The fund's name or fees are out of range.
funds.refusal.fundTerms.why: A name takes 3 to 30 characters. Fees have ceilings: the management fee is at most 2% a game year, and the performance fee at most 20%.
funds.refusal.fundTerms.do: Change the name or the fees, then try again.
funds.refusal.fundRank.what: Running a fund needs the Operator rank (R3).
funds.refusal.fundRank.why: A fund is run by a player who holds the derivatives licence and the capital to back it.
funds.refusal.fundRank.do: Keep trading until you reach R3. The Exchange shows the rank you need.
funds.refusal.fundAge.what: Your account is too new to run a fund.
funds.refusal.fundAge.why: A manager's account must be at least 14 game days old.
funds.refusal.fundAge.do: Wait until the account is old enough, then open the fund.
funds.refusal.fundBanned.what: A court verdict bans you from running a fund.
funds.refusal.fundBanned.why: A fund-abuse verdict stops fund management until its ban runs out.
funds.refusal.fundBanned.do: Wait for the ban to lift. It ends 8 real weeks after the verdict.
funds.refusal.fundConviction.what: A fund-abuse verdict blocks a new fund.
funds.refusal.fundConviction.why: The verdict is within the last 8 real weeks.
funds.refusal.fundConviction.do: Wait until 8 real weeks have passed since the verdict.
funds.refusal.fundOwnsOne.why: A manager runs one open fund at a time.
funds.refusal.fundOwnsOne.do: Keep your current fund. A second one can open once it has closed.
funds.refusal.fundStake.why: A fund starts with a stake of at least $250,000 from its manager, who keeps at least 10% of it.
funds.refusal.fundStake.do: Put at least $250,000 into the stake.
funds.refusal.fundCash.what: You do not have enough spendable cash.
funds.refusal.fundCash.why: Restricted cash cannot fund a fund.
funds.refusal.fundCash.do: Free up cash, or enter a smaller amount.
funds.refusal.fundClosed.what: This fund is winding down or closed.
funds.refusal.fundClosed.why: A fund being wound down takes no new money and no trades.
funds.refusal.fundClosed.do: Pick a fund that is open, or redeem what you hold.
funds.refusal.fundFrozen.why: Its manager has been away for 72 real hours, so trading is off.
funds.refusal.fundFrozen.do: Redemptions are open without the gate. Redeem your units, or wait for the manager to return.
funds.refusal.fundBreaker.what: The fund is in its breaker.
funds.refusal.fundBreaker.why: Its NAV fell 30% from its one-week high, so new trades pause for one game day.
funds.refusal.fundBreaker.do: Wait for the breaker to lift, then trade again.
funds.refusal.fundMandate.what: That asset is outside the fund's mandate.
funds.refusal.fundMandate.why: The mandate names the asset classes the fund may trade.
funds.refusal.fundMandate.do: Trade an asset in a class the mandate names, or change the mandate (24 real hours of notice).
funds.refusal.fundLeverage.what: That trade would take the fund past its leverage limit.
funds.refusal.fundLeverage.why: Gross exposure may not exceed the mandate's leverage: 1.5 times equity at most.
funds.refusal.fundLeverage.do: Trade a smaller quantity, or sell first.
funds.refusal.fundPosition.what: That position is more than the mandate allows.
funds.refusal.fundPosition.why: One position may be at most 20% of NAV, or the lower limit the mandate sets.
funds.refusal.fundInsiderCap.what: This asset is capped for the fund.
funds.refusal.fundInsiderCap.why: The manager is an insider of it or holds 1% of its float, so the fund may hold at most 5% of its NAV in it.
funds.refusal.fundInsiderCap.do: Trade a smaller quantity in this asset.
funds.refusal.fundSelfMatch.what: The fund cannot cross an open order.
funds.refusal.fundSelfMatch.why: The manager or a linked account has an opposite open order in this asset.
funds.refusal.fundSelfMatch.do: Cancel that order, or wait for it to fill.
funds.refusal.fundOrderRejected.why: The quantity or the fund's cash does not cover the order.
funds.refusal.fundOrderRejected.do: Check the quantity and the fund's cash, then send it again.
funds.refusal.fundInvestorAge.what: Your account is too new to invest in a fund.
funds.refusal.fundInvestorAge.why: An investor's account must be at least 7 real days old.
funds.refusal.fundInvestorAge.do: Wait until the account is old enough.
funds.refusal.fundInvestorLink.what: You cannot invest in this fund.
funds.refusal.fundInvestorLink.why: You are linked to its manager.
funds.refusal.fundInvestorLimit.what: This deposit would take you past your limit in the fund.
funds.refusal.fundInvestorLimit.why: A fund may hold at most 25% of your net worth.
funds.refusal.fundStakeLow.what: The manager's stake would fall too low.
funds.refusal.fundStakeLow.why: While investors are in the fund, the manager keeps at least 10% of it and $250,000. Deposits pause until the stake is back above that floor.
funds.refusal.fundStakeLow.do: Wait for the stake to be restored. If you are the manager, redeem a smaller amount.
funds.refusal.fundAumCap.what: The fund is at its AUM cap.
funds.refusal.fundAumCap.why: AUM may be at most 10 times the manager's stake, and $10M in the fund's first 14 real days.
funds.refusal.fundAumCap.do: Invest a smaller amount, or wait for the cap to lift.
funds.refusal.fundRedeem.why: You can redeem only units you hold, in a positive amount. A manager's stake may not fall below the floor while investors are in.
funds.refusal.fundRedeem.do: Enter a smaller number of units than you hold.
funds.refusal.fundMandateInvalid.why: A mandate names at least one asset class, a leverage from 1x to 1.5x, and a position cap of 20% of NAV or less.
funds.refusal.fundMandateInvalid.do: Fix the mandate, then send it again.
funds.refusal.fundTradeInvalid.why: An order is a buy or a sell, with a positive quantity, and a limit price on a limit order.
funds.refusal.fundTradeInvalid.do: Fix the order, then send it again.
funds.order.cancelledLinked: An open order of {fund} was cancelled: an account linked to you now stands opposite it, and a fund may not match a linked account.
company.refusal.ipoFilings.what: The IPO needs three filed quarters.
company.refusal.ipoFilings.why: A listing is priced on filed numbers, and the market wants a track record of three quarters.
company.refusal.ipoFilings.do: File three quarters, then request the IPO again.
company.refusal.ipoValue.what: The company is worth less than the IPO minimum.
company.refusal.ipoValue.why: Its engine value must reach the minimum before a listing is priced.
company.refusal.ipoValue.do: Grow the company's value, then request the IPO again.
company.refusal.ipoRank.what: The IPO needs the Operator rank or higher.
company.refusal.ipoRank.why: Only founders at Operator rank can take a company public.
company.refusal.ipoRank.do: Keep growing your net worth until you reach Operator.
company.refusal.ipoConviction.what: The IPO is blocked by a recent conviction.
company.refusal.ipoConviction.why: A conviction for fund abuse blocks listings for eight weeks.
company.refusal.ipoConviction.do: Wait out the eight weeks, then request the IPO.
company.refusal.ipoCovenant.what: The IPO is blocked by a covenant.
company.refusal.ipoCovenant.why: A company in breach or in cure cannot list.
company.refusal.ipoCovenant.do: Cure the covenant, then request the IPO again.
company.refusal.ipoFloatOutOfBand.what: That float is outside the allowed range.
company.refusal.ipoFloatOutOfBand.why: The float must be between {min} and {max} of the shares after the IPO.
company.refusal.ipoFloatOutOfBand.do: Choose a float inside the range.
company.refusal.ipoAlreadyRequested.what: An IPO is already requested for this company.
company.refusal.ipoAlreadyRequested.why: Only one IPO book can be open at a time.
company.refusal.ipoAlreadyRequested.do: Wait for the book to list, or check its price.
company.refusal.ipoBookClosed.why: Subscriptions are taken only on the day the book opens.
company.refusal.ipoBookClosed.do: Request the IPO again to open a new book.
company.refusal.ipoOwnerSet.what: You cannot buy in your own company's IPO.
company.refusal.ipoOwnerSet.why: The founder and any linked account are kept out of the book.
company.refusal.ipoOwnerSet.do: Let other players buy, or keep your shares.
company.refusal.ipoAccountTooYoung.what: That account is too new for the IPO book.
company.refusal.ipoAccountTooYoung.why: Accounts under {minDays} game days old are not allocated shares.
company.refusal.ipoAccountTooYoung.do: Wait until the account is older.
company.refusal.ipoBadShares.what: The number of shares is not valid.
company.refusal.ipoBadShares.why: A subscription needs a whole number of shares above zero.
company.refusal.ipoBadShares.do: Enter a whole number of shares.
company.refusal.alreadyListed.why: A listed company trades on the exchange, not through the IPO book.
company.refusal.alreadyListed.do: Trade its stock on the Exchange.
company.refusal.planSellOnly.why: Trading plans are sell-only: buys and short sales are never scheduled.
company.refusal.planSellOnly.do: Place buy orders inside the open trading window.
company.refusal.planFloorTooHigh.what: The minimum sell price is too high.
company.refusal.planFloorTooHigh.why: It can be at most 80% of the commit-day close, which is {maxFloor}.
company.refusal.planFloorTooHigh.do: Set the minimum at {maxFloor} or below, then commit again.
company.refusal.planLimit.what: You already have two live plans in this company.
company.refusal.planLimit.why: Each founder can run at most two plans per company.
company.refusal.planLimit.do: Let one plan end, then commit a new one.
company.refusal.planInLockup.what: A plan day falls inside the lockup.
company.refusal.planInLockup.why: Founder shares cannot be sold until the lockup ends.
company.refusal.planInLockup.do: Start the plan after the lockup.
company.refusal.planTooSoon.why: A plan is committed at least 63 game days before its first day.
company.refusal.planTooSoon.do: Start the plan on day {earliestDay} or later.
company.refusal.planUnfunded.what: You do not hold enough shares for this plan.
company.refusal.planUnfunded.why: The plan locks every share it will sell. You are {shortfall} shares short.
company.refusal.planUnfunded.do: Buy the shares inside the window, or make the plan smaller.
company.refusal.planBanned.what: Plans are banned for this founder.
company.refusal.planBanned.why: A breach put a ban on new plans until day {untilDay}.
company.refusal.planImmutable.what: A committed plan cannot be changed.
company.refusal.planImmutable.why: A plan is fixed at commit, so there is no edit or cancel.
company.refusal.planImmutable.do: Let the plan run to its end. Its shares stay locked until then.
company.refusal.planBadSpec.what: The plan's terms are not valid.
company.refusal.planBadSpec.why: Days must be ascending whole days, with a positive size and price.
company.refusal.planBadSpec.do: Check the days, the size and the minimum price.
company.refusal.planExists.what: A plan with this id already exists.
company.refusal.planExists.why: Each plan has its own id.
company.refusal.planOverCap.what: The plan sells too many shares a day.
company.refusal.planOverCap.why: A founder can sell at most 2% of the shares outstanding a game day, which is {maxPerDay} shares.
company.refusal.planOverCap.do: Lower the daily size to {maxPerDay} shares or below.
company.refusal.planNotListed.what: The company is not listed yet.
company.refusal.planNotListed.why: Plans and buybacks need a listed stock.
company.refusal.buybackBadSpec.why: A buyback needs a whole size, a range of days, and a whole number of shares a day.
company.refusal.buybackBadSpec.do: Check the size and the days, then file again.
company.refusal.buybackTooLarge.what: The buyback buys too much a day.
company.refusal.buybackTooLarge.why: A buyback is at most 1% of the float a game day, which is {maxPerDay} shares.
company.refusal.buybackTooLarge.do: Lower the daily size, or spread the buyback over more days.
company.refusal.buybackNotFilingDay.what: Buybacks are filed on one day only.
company.refusal.buybackNotFilingDay.why: A buyback is filed the day after the company's filing, which is day {filingDay}.
company.refusal.buybackClosedWindow.what: The buyback falls outside the trading window.
company.refusal.buybackClosedWindow.why: A buyback runs only inside the window, from two days after the filing to twenty-one days after it.
company.refusal.buybackImmutable.what: A buyback program cannot be changed.
company.refusal.buybackImmutable.why: A buyback is fixed once it is filed.
company.refusal.buybackImmutable.do: Let the program run to its end.
company.refusal.buybackCovenant.what: The buyback is blocked by a covenant.
company.refusal.buybackCovenant.why: The covenant is in {covenant}, and a breach or a cure blocks buybacks.
company.refusal.buybackCovenant.do: Cure the covenant, then file on the next filing day.
company.refusal.buybackLeverage.what: The buyback would push leverage too high.
company.refusal.buybackLeverage.why: Net debt over EBITDA must stay at {maxLeverage} or below after the buyback.
company.refusal.buybackLeverage.do: Pay down debt, or file a smaller buyback.
company.refusal.buybackCash.what: The company does not have the cash for this buyback.
company.refusal.buybackCash.why: A buyback is paid from company cash. You are {shortfall} short.
company.refusal.buybackCash.do: Wait until the company has the cash, or file a smaller buyback.
company.refusal.loanTier.what: The company is too small for a loan.
company.refusal.loanTier.do: Grow the company to the {minTier} tier.
company.refusal.loanCovenant.what: A loan is blocked by a covenant.
company.refusal.loanBadAmount.what: That loan amount is not valid.
company.refusal.loanBadAmount.why: A loan needs an amount above zero.
company.refusal.loanBankCash.what: The bank cannot lend that much.
company.refusal.loanBankCash.why: The bank has {available} available to lend.
company.refusal.guaranteeNotAcknowledged: If the company defaults, you owe {personalDebt} personally.
Read the consequence, then confirm the guarantee.
company.refusal.repayBadAmount.why: A repayment needs an amount above zero.
company.refusal.dividendNotPermitted.why: It needs retained earnings above zero after it, 21 game days of costs in cash, clean covenants, and a total at most the TTM free cash flow.
company.refusal.dividendNotPermitted.do: Lower the dividend, or wait for the next filing.
company.refusal.dividendBadAmount.why: A dividend needs an amount per share above zero.
company.refusal.dividendBadAmount.do: Enter a positive amount per share.

shop.none: Buy a business to start running it here.
shop.wellRun: Well run means crew {crew}, quality {quality}, maintained, price {price}x. At those settings a shop pays back in about {days} game days.
shop.overdraft.title: Your cash is below zero.
shop.overdraft.body: Running costs are still due each game day and keep coming out of cash. Sell a shop or move cash in to clear it.
shop.overdraft.inbox: {name}’s running costs took your cash below zero. Sell a shop or move cash in to clear it.

shop.price.capped: Above your manager’s {cap}x cap. The price drops to {cap}x on the next game day.

shop.price.hint: A higher price earns more on each sale and wins fewer customers.
shop.quality.hint: Better inputs lift revenue and reviews, at a daily cost.

shop.maintained.hint: A maintained shop holds its condition at 100 for a daily fee. Without maintenance, the shop wears down.

lp.refuse.dead.why: A token with no trade for 24 game days, or with its curve cash too low for a week, is dead. Its curve still pays sellers.
lp.refuse.dead.do: Sell what you hold, or pick a live token.
lp.refuse.graduated.why: The curve is closed. The token now trades on the exchange, against its liquidity book.
lp.refuse.graduated.do: Trade it in the Broker, or from the Graduated tab.
lp.refuse.buzzCap.what: This token already has its promos for today.
lp.refuse.buzzCap.why: A token takes at most {max} buzz items a game day.
lp.refuse.buzzCap.do: Try again tomorrow, or buy a different kind of promo.
lp.refuse.cash.what: You do not have enough cash.
lp.refuse.cash.why: This needs ${need}, and your cash does not cover it.
lp.refuse.cash.do: Sell something, or pick a smaller amount.
lp.refuse.adCashOps.what: Ad cash can’t pay for this.
lp.refuse.adCashOps.why: Launchpad buzz and launch fees are ops, and ad cash is barred from ops for 72 hours.
lp.refuse.adCashOps.do: Use cash that is past its hold.
lp.refuse.zero.why: A trade needs a positive amount: dollars to spend, or whole tokens to sell.
lp.refuse.zero.do: Enter a positive number and try again.
lp.refuse.holdings.what: You do not hold that many tokens.
lp.refuse.holdings.do: Enter a quantity up to what you hold.
lp.refuse.locked.why: {locked} of your tokens stay locked until the vesting ends on game day {day}.
lp.refuse.locked.do: Sell only the unlocked tokens, or wait for the next unlock.
lp.refuse.slippage.what: The fill would be worse than your limit.
lp.refuse.slippage.why: It would move the price by {slip}, and your maximum is {max}.
lp.refuse.slippage.do: Trade a smaller amount, or raise the maximum slippage.
lp.refuse.creatorCap.what: The creator cap would be exceeded.
lp.refuse.creatorCap.why: The creator and linked accounts may hold at most 10% of supply on the curve. {room} tokens are left.
lp.refuse.creatorCap.do: Buy fewer tokens, or leave this token to other players.
lp.refuse.sold.why: Its last tokens have sold, and the token is graduating.
lp.refuse.sold.do: Trade it in the Broker once it has graduated.
lp.refuse.tooSmall.why: The amount buys less than one token at this price.
lp.refuse.tooLarge.what: That sell is more than the curve can take.
lp.refuse.tooLarge.why: A curve cannot hold more tokens than it has sold.
lp.refuse.noPlayer.why: A launch or a trade needs an account in the world.
lp.refuse.noPlayer.do: Sign in, join, then try again.
lp.refuse.noFlag.why: A case needs a public flag: the creator sold half their holding after graduation, or sold 3% of supply in a day while the price fell 40%.

lp.refuse.ownFlag.what: You cannot sue over your own token.
lp.refuse.ownFlag.why: The creator and their linked accounts cannot file against their own token.
lp.refuse.ownFlag.do: Pick a token you did not create.
lp.refuse.notEligible.what: You did not buy {ticker} in the window before the dump.
lp.refuse.notEligible.why: A case needs a purchase in the 7 game days before the flag.
lp.refuse.notEligible.do: Only holders from that window can file.
lp.refuse.alreadySued.what: You already have a case over {ticker}.
lp.refuse.alreadySued.why: There is one case per token and holder.
lp.refuse.alreadySued.do: Follow the case in Legal & Court.
lp.refuse.rank.what: You need the rank Hustler to launch.
lp.refuse.rank.why: Launches are for players at Hustler or above.
lp.refuse.rank.do: Earn your next rank, then launch.
lp.refuse.age.what: Your account is too new to launch.

ad.refusal.adNotOffered.why: Breaks are offered when the cash and the net worth were under $1,000 at the start of the day.
ad.refusal.adAge.what: The account is too new for a break.
ad.refusal.adAge.why: Breaks open a real day after the account starts.
ad.refusal.adCap.what: You have used today’s ten breaks.
ad.refusal.adCap.why: The limit is per profile, so linked accounts share it.
ad.refusal.adBusy.why: One card runs at a time.
ad.refusal.adNoBreak.what: That break is not open any more.
ad.refusal.adNoBreak.why: It has closed, or it was already used.
ad.refusal.adNoBreak.do: Start a new one from the card.
ad.refusal.adTooSoon.why: A full watch needs 15 seconds, and a skip needs 5.
ad.refusal.adTooSoon.do: Keep watching, or wait for the skip.

ad.refusal.adCashMargin.why: A buy past your cash borrows, and ad cash is held for 72 hours.
ad.refusal.adCashMargin.do: Buy within your other cash, or sell first.
ad.refusal.adCashDerivative.why: Options are derivatives, and ad cash is held for 72 hours.

ad.refusal.adCashTransfer.what: Ad cash can’t leave your account.

comeback.refusal.comebackClosing.do: Wait for the new chapter to open.

comeback.refusal.comebackMarginBlock.do: Buy within your cash, or sell first. Margin returns after 14 days.

eca.notice.what: The Exchange Conduct Authority (ECA) has opened an inquiry into your trading in {ticker}.
eca.notice.why: Your orders in this stock have drawn routine surveillance. An inquiry is a review, not a finding.
eca.notice.do: Keep your records. Nothing is frozen while the inquiry is open, and you need do nothing else yet.
eca.investigation.what: The ECA has moved its inquiry into your trading in {ticker} to a full investigation.
eca.investigation.why: The review found a pattern that needs more evidence before the regulator can decide. It is not a finding yet.
eca.investigation.do: Keep your records and answer any request from the ECA. A decision is made by a tribunal, never by the market.
eca.verdict.convicted.what: The tribunal found that your trading in {ticker} was market abuse.
eca.verdict.convicted.why: The evidence met the tribunal's bar. Your reputation has fallen, and the fine is a sink, not a payment to anyone.
eca.verdict.convicted.do: Pay the fine of ${fine} and give up ${disgorged} of gains. Both come out of your cash.
eca.verdict.cleared.what: The tribunal did not find market abuse in your trading in {ticker}.
eca.verdict.cleared.why: The tribunal heard the file and did not convict. The file is closed, and a new inquiry cannot open for 20 game days.
eca.verdict.cleared.do: No payment is due. You can keep trading; the ECA can reopen the review if the pattern returns.

auction.unsold: {item} did not sell. No cash moved.

insurance.unpaid: The insurer could not pay your {cause} claim.
sixd.refuse.noPlayer.what: There is no player account to act with.
sixd.refuse.noPlayer.why: Only a joined player can do this, and this session has no account.
sixd.refuse.noPlayer.do: Join the world first, then try again.
sixd.refuse.insBreach.what: Insurance cannot go on during a breach.
sixd.refuse.insBreach.why: A hostile session is open on your systems, and a policy bought now would cover a loss already in progress.
sixd.refuse.insBreach.do: Cut the hostile session in Security, then wait 24 hours before you switch insurance on.
sixd.refuse.insLockout.why: You were breached within the last 24 hours, and the switch waits that long after the last breach.
sixd.refuse.insLockout.do: Wait, then switch insurance on in Settings, Security.
sixd.refuse.insNothing.what: There is nothing to insure yet.
sixd.refuse.insNothing.why: Insurance covers collectibles and shops. A policy on nothing would have no value to cover.
sixd.refuse.insNothing.do: Buy a collectible in the Boutique or a shop in Businesses, then switch insurance on.
sixd.refuse.auctionNoLot.what: That lot is not on offer this week.
sixd.refuse.auctionNoLot.why: Lots change each real week, and this one is not on this week's list.
sixd.refuse.auctionNoLot.do: Pick a lot from this week's auction list.
sixd.refuse.auctionOpenLeft.what: The lots cannot open with that window.
sixd.refuse.auctionOpenLeft.why: An auction runs one real hour at most, and the window must hold at least one tick.
sixd.refuse.auctionOpenLeft.do: Pass a window of 1 to 720 ticks, or leave it out for the full hour.
sixd.refuse.streakAccent.what: That is not a streak accent.
sixd.refuse.streakAccent.why: Only the three accent palettes come with a streak milestone: phosphor, riviera and broadsheet.
sixd.refuse.streakAccent.do: Name one of those three accents.
sixd.refuse.auctionNotYet.why: Bids open with the week, in {hours} hours.
sixd.refuse.auctionNotYet.do: Come back when the week opens.
sixd.refuse.auctionClosed.why: An auction runs one real hour, and a lot that has ended keeps its result.
sixd.refuse.auctionClosed.do: Look at the lot for its result, or wait for next week's lots.
sixd.refuse.auctionRank.why: Collectibles unlock by rank, as they do in the Boutique.
sixd.refuse.auctionAmount.why: A bid must be a positive number of dollars.
sixd.refuse.auctionAmount.do: Type an amount above zero, at or above the minimum shown.
sixd.refuse.bidLow.what: Your bid is below the minimum.
sixd.refuse.bidLow.why: The next bid must be at least ${min}.
sixd.refuse.bidLow.do: Raise the bid to at least ${min}.
sixd.refuse.bidCash.what: Not enough cash for that bid.
sixd.refuse.bidCash.why: A bid of ${amount} needs ${need} in spendable cash, buyer premium included.
sixd.refuse.bidCash.do: Lower the bid, or free up cash first.
sixd.refuse.streakClaimed.why: One claim per real day. The next one opens with tomorrow's login.
sixd.refuse.streakLogin.what: The streak needs a login today.
sixd.refuse.streakLogin.why: The streak counts real days with a login and one action.
sixd.refuse.streakLogin.do: Log in today, then claim again.
sixd.refuse.streakAction.what: The streak needs one action today.
sixd.refuse.streakAction.why: A trade, a bid or a purchase counts as today's action. A refused one does not.
sixd.refuse.tnRank.what: The tournament runs on AI Lab models, and your lab opens at {rank}.
sixd.refuse.tnRank.why: The entry is your best trading model, and models come from the lab.
sixd.refuse.tnRank.do: Reach {rank}, train a trading model, then enter.
sixd.refuse.tnNoModel.what: You have no trading model to enter.
sixd.refuse.tnNoModel.why: The entry is your best trading model, and you have not trained one.
sixd.refuse.tnNoModel.do: Train a trading model in the AI Lab, then enter.
sixd.refuse.tnNoBot.what: Your best model runs no bot.
sixd.refuse.tnNoBot.why: An entry trades through a bot, and {model} has none deployed.
sixd.refuse.tnNoBot.do: Deploy a bot on {model} in the AI Lab, then enter.
sixd.refuse.tnEntered.why: One entry a week. It locks at tick {lock}.
sixd.refuse.tnEntered.do: Wait for the next week's entries.
sixd.refuse.tnNoWeek.why: Nobody entered that week, so there is nothing to settle.
sixd.refuse.tnNoWeek.do: Check the current week on the tournament board.
sixd.refuse.tnSettled.why: A settled week's seeds are public, and its rows are final.
sixd.refuse.tnNotLocked.do: Settle the week after it locks.
sixd.refuse.tnCommit.what: The seeds do not match week {week}'s commitment.
sixd.refuse.tnCommit.why: A settlement must use the seeds committed at the week's open, or it is refused.
sixd.refuse.tnCommit.do: Run the week from its committed seeds.
sixd.refuse.tnRowUnknown.what: A row is not an entry of this week.
sixd.refuse.tnRowUnknown.why: Settlement rows name only this week's entries and the house AIs.
sixd.refuse.tnRowUnknown.do: Run the week again from its entries.
sixd.refuse.tnRowHouse.what: A house row is not a house AI.
sixd.refuse.tnRowHouse.why: House rows must name one of the five house strategies.
sixd.refuse.tnRowHouse.do: Run the week again from the house AIs.
sixd.refuse.tnLogOptOut.what: No trade log is published for this entry.
sixd.refuse.tnLogOptOut.why: A trade log is published only for an entrant who opted in at entry.
sixd.refuse.tnLogOptOut.do: Opt in when you enter, so a log can be published if you finish top three.
sixd.refuse.tnLogTop.what: This entry is not in the top three.
sixd.refuse.tnLogTop.why: A trade log is published only for a top-three entry that opted in.
sixd.refuse.tnLogTop.do: There is nothing to publish for this entry this week.
sixd.refuse.tnServerOnly.what: Only the server settles a tournament.
sixd.refuse.tnServerOnly.why: The server runs a settlement off the tick loop, and players cannot send one.
sixd.refuse.tnServerOnly.do: Nothing to do here. The week settles when it locks.

sixd.ins.title: Insurance
sixd.ins.intro: One switch covers your collectibles and shops against hacks, fires, thefts and losses. A weekly premium of 0.4% of what you insure. A 10% excess on each claim, and a claim pays at most 80% of its loss.
sixd.streak.title: Daily streak
sixd.streak.intro: Log in and take one action each real day, then claim. Fixed rewards, no nags. One rest day a week keeps half your streak.
sixd.auc.title: This week's auctions
sixd.auc.intro: Up to five rare collectibles, sold by English auction over one real hour. A bid in the last two minutes adds two minutes. The high bid and the count are public during the auction; bidders show at the end.
sixd.auc.reserveMet: The high bid met the reserve.
sixd.auc.reserveNotMet: The reserve was not met, so the lot did not sell.
